opening.title: A Seat at the Table
opening.body: A quiet corner, a few cards, a story to share. Use these Minecraft scenes for readings and roleplay. Tap a name to jump; the links below each page will bring you back.

how_to.title: A Deck in Hand
how_to.body: Use a deck to draw its top card. Sneak-use to shuffle. To return a card, hold it in your offhand and sneak-use the deck. Otherwise, keep your offhand clear while handling cards.

how_to.title: Around the Table
how_to.body: Use a loose card on a clear, flat surface to lay it face-down. Use it to flip; sneak-use to rotate. Empty-hand hit picks it up. Hit with a deck to return it; sneak-hit gathers nearby cards.

reading.title: Make a Little Reading
reading.body: Try a card for a character, place or choice, or three for a story. Meanings are invitations, never predictions or powers. Deal blind: /trigger tarot.action set 5. This guide is optional.

sections.title: Major Arcana
sections.intro: Large turning points, seen through the places and choices of a Minecraft life.

entries.name: The Fool
entries.body: The path ends at an unexplored valley. The Fool carries curiosity before certainty: give your character a beginning, and consider what they bring along.

entries.name: The Magician
entries.body: Tools lie ready around a crafting table. The Magician turns an idea into deliberate action: which skill could your character put to use with what is here?

entries.name: The High Priestess
entries.body: Behind the bookshelf, a quiet room keeps its secrets. The High Priestess invites listening and patient attention before your character names what they know.

entries.name: The Empress
entries.body: Wheat, flowers and bees crowd a well-tended garden. The Empress suggests care that makes room for growth, including the pleasure of enjoying what flourishes.

entries.name: The Emperor
entries.body: A keep stands because its foundations and boundaries hold. The Emperor asks how your character creates order, and whether that order shelters other people.

entries.name: The Hierophant
entries.body: At the village lectern, an old method passes to a new pair of hands. The Hierophant explores shared customs: what is worth learning, keeping or questioning?

entries.name: The Lovers
entries.body: Two paths meet beside a home built together. The Lovers invites a choice shaped by values and affection: what would your character willingly commit to?

entries.name: The Chariot
entries.body: Two rails pull toward different destinations. The Chariot is the effort of choosing a course and guiding competing impulses toward one purposeful journey.

entries.name: Strength
entries.body: A startled horse needs a steady hand, not a louder voice. Strength imagines courage expressed through patience, restraint and kindness toward the difficult.

entries.name: The Hermit
entries.body: One lantern lights a hilltop far from the village noise. The Hermit makes space for a private question, and for returning with something carefully understood.

entries.name: Wheel of Fortune
entries.body: Planting, harvest and bare soil take their turns. The Wheel holds changing circumstances: how does your character respond when the season will not stay still?

entries.name: Justice
entries.body: A shared chest needs an honest account of what went in and out. Justice asks your character to weigh evidence, accept consequences and make a fair repair.

entries.name: The Hanged Man
entries.body: From beneath a bridge, the familiar river looks different. The Hanged Man offers a willing pause: what becomes visible when your character stops pushing?

entries.name: Death
entries.body: An old base stands empty as its builders move on. Death gives an ending its proper weight, making room for another chapter without pretending nothing was lost.

entries.name: Temperance
entries.body: Two streams join without losing all their differences. Temperance explores adjustment and proportion: which parts of your character's life could work together?

entries.name: The Devil
entries.body: A treasure room becomes a prison when leaving feels impossible. The Devil asks what bargain, appetite or habit your character keeps choosing at a hidden cost.

entries.name: The Tower
entries.body: A spire built on weak stone breaks open. The Tower brings a story's false certainty down: once the dust settles, what truth can the builders no longer ignore?

entries.name: The Star
entries.body: After the wreckage, someone repairs the village well. The Star offers modest hope through renewal: a small act can make the future feel worth tending again.

entries.name: The Moon
entries.body: Reeds and moonlight blur the marsh path. The Moon lets uncertainty enter the story; give your character time to distinguish a fear, a guess and a real clue.

entries.name: The Sun
entries.body: Sunlight fills a courtyard where nobody needs to hide their delight. The Sun celebrates openness, simple pleasures and the warmth of being welcomed as you are.

entries.name: Judgement
entries.body: The village bell calls people out to answer for an unfinished story. Judgement invites an honest reckoning, and a decision about who your character means to become.

entries.name: The World
entries.body: The last map joins the wall and the whole landscape comes into view. The World marks completion: let your character recognize the journey before setting out again.

sections.title: Wands
sections.intro: Sparks, ventures and the effort of bringing an idea into the world.

entries.name: Ace of Wands
entries.body: A torch catches beside an empty building plot. The Ace of Wands is the spark of an undertaking, still small enough to need a willing hand and a little shelter.

entries.name: Two of Wands
entries.body: From a watchtower, your character studies two routes on a map. The Two of Wands holds ambition at the planning stage: choose how far this venture should reach.

entries.name: Three of Wands
entries.body: Boats leave the dock carrying work already begun. The Three of Wands looks outward, asking how your character waits, prepares and welcomes a wider horizon.

entries.name: Four of Wands
entries.body: Lanterns hang above a finished village arch. The Four of Wands celebrates a shared milestone and the welcome that turns a structure into somewhere to belong.

entries.name: Five of Wands
entries.body: Five builders reach for the same patch of wall. The Five of Wands explores clashing ideas, playful rivalry and the work of finding room for everyone to contribute.

entries.name: Six of Wands
entries.body: A banner rises for the explorer coming home. The Six of Wands enjoys recognition, while asking whose quiet help belongs in the story of this public success.

entries.name: Seven of Wands
entries.body: On a narrow rampart, your character defends a hard-won position. The Seven of Wands asks which conviction deserves that effort when agreement is no longer easy.

entries.name: Eight of Wands
entries.body: Arrows cross the sky before anyone can call them back. The Eight of Wands gives a scene speed: messages arrive, plans move and a timely response suddenly matters.

entries.name: Nine of Wands
entries.body: A repaired fence bears the marks of earlier raids. The Nine of Wands holds tired resolve, asking what protection is useful and what support a watchkeeper needs.

entries.name: Ten of Wands
entries.body: Every slot is full and the walk home feels longer. The Ten of Wands explores responsibility carried too far: which task could your character share or set down?

entries.name: Page of Wands
entries.body: A new explorer stops to sketch an unfamiliar biome. The Page of Wands brings eager curiosity, trying an interest before knowing whether it will become a calling.

entries.name: Knight of Wands
entries.body: A rider races toward the next unfamiliar hill. The Knight of Wands brings daring and restless momentum; give that enthusiasm a destination worth staying for.

entries.name: Queen of Wands
entries.body: Beside a bright hearth, a confident host makes newcomers feel included. The Queen of Wands expresses warmth that encourages others without needing to dim itself.

entries.name: King of Wands
entries.body: A leader sees a settlement where others see an empty plain. The King of Wands gives a vision direction, inviting others to help shape how it becomes real.

sections.title: Cups
sections.intro: Affection, imagination and the many ways people find connection.

entries.name: Ace of Cups
entries.body: A spring breaks through dry ground beside the path. The Ace of Cups opens space for affection, wonder or a creative feeling your character has yet to put into words.

entries.name: Two of Cups
entries.body: Two travelers make room at one campfire. The Two of Cups begins with mutual recognition: what can these characters offer freely, and receive with equal respect?

entries.name: Three of Cups
entries.body: Three friends bring different dishes to the picnic table. The Three of Cups enjoys companionship, shared celebration and the ease of having people to laugh with.

entries.name: Four of Cups
entries.body: An offered bowl sits beside someone lost in thought. The Four of Cups allows discontent and withdrawal, while asking what invitation your character may be overlooking.

entries.name: Five of Cups
entries.body: Water spills from three buckets; two still stand nearby. The Five of Cups gives disappointment room, then gently asks what connection or possibility remains intact.

entries.name: Six of Cups
entries.body: An old treehouse still holds the sign you made together. The Six of Cups explores familiar kindness, remembered joys and what the past can offer without becoming home.

entries.name: Seven of Cups
entries.body: Every market stall offers a different imagined life. The Seven of Cups explores tempting possibilities: which desire can your character name clearly enough to choose?

entries.name: Eight of Cups
entries.body: A boat waits beside a comfortable home that no longer feels right. The Eight of Cups follows the difficult choice to leave something valued in search of deeper meaning.

entries.name: Nine of Cups
entries.body: A favorite supper waits in a room arranged just so. The Nine of Cups savors personal contentment: let your character enjoy enough without needing another prize.

entries.name: Ten of Cups
entries.body: A long table has a place for every member of the village. The Ten of Cups imagines lasting belonging, where shared happiness includes the work of caring for one another.

entries.name: Page of Cups
entries.body: A young artist sketches an unexpected fish at the pond. The Page of Cups welcomes a tender idea or surprising feeling before deciding whether it makes practical sense.

entries.name: Knight of Cups
entries.body: A traveler brings flowers and a carefully rehearsed invitation. The Knight of Cups follows an ideal of beauty or affection, asking how that promise meets another person.

entries.name: Queen of Cups
entries.body: At the window seat, a listener leaves room for an unfinished story. The Queen of Cups offers emotional attention, with enough boundaries to keep kindness freely given.

entries.name: King of Cups
entries.body: A harbor keeper holds a steady course through a quarrel. The King of Cups imagines feeling deeply while choosing a measured response that others can safely answer.

sections.title: Swords
sections.intro: Thoughts, truths and conflicts that ask for careful attention.

entries.name: Ace of Swords
entries.body: One clean cut frees a tangled lead. The Ace of Swords offers a clear thought, a truthful sentence or a decision that separates the real issue from its distractions.

entries.name: Two of Swords
entries.body: Two roads wait beyond a gate your character keeps shut. The Two of Swords explores an uneasy stalemate: what information or feeling has been kept outside the decision?

entries.name: Three of Swords
entries.body: A shared sign is split by words that cannot be unsaid. The Three of Swords makes room for hurt and difficult truth, without requiring the story to hurry past either.

entries.name: Four of Swords
entries.body: Armor rests beside a bed in a quiet room. The Four of Swords gives a conflict an interval: your character can step away before choosing what deserves their next effort.

entries.name: Five of Swords
entries.body: The winner stands alone in an emptied arena. The Five of Swords questions a victory bought with trust: what did the argument cost beyond the point that was won?

entries.name: Six of Swords
entries.body: A boat carries a tired group toward a quieter shore. The Six of Swords marks a transition that brings old concerns along, even as distance makes a new beginning possible.

entries.name: Seven of Swords
entries.body: A hidden tunnel offers a way around the guarded gate. The Seven of Swords explores strategy and concealment: who benefits from this secret, and who bears its cost?

entries.name: Eight of Swords
entries.body: A traveler sees only the fences nearby. The Eight of Swords explores a sense of restriction, inviting a closer look at which limits are real and which are assumed.

entries.name: Nine of Swords
entries.body: A character watches the dark through a bedroom window. The Nine of Swords gives worry a voice in the story, and asks what changes when that worry is finally spoken.

entries.name: Ten of Swords
entries.body: At a ruined outpost, a failed plan has ended. The Ten of Swords names the finality of a defeat, leaving your character free to stop defending what is already over.

entries.name: Page of Swords
entries.body: A scout pauses over unfamiliar tracks. The Page of Swords brings questions and alert observation, learning to check a suspicion before repeating it as fact.

entries.name: Knight of Swords
entries.body: A messenger races ahead with an urgent argument. The Knight of Swords commits fiercely to an idea, asking whether speed has left room to hear the people in its path.

entries.name: Queen of Swords
entries.body: A village judge listens, then draws a boundary. The Queen of Swords combines discernment with hard-earned honesty, allowing compassion without blurring what is true.

entries.name: King of Swords
entries.body: At the council table, a leader explains the reasons for a ruling. The King of Swords uses authority through clear standards, tested evidence and accountable decisions.

sections.title: Pentacles
sections.intro: Work, resources and the ordinary care that makes a life livable.

entries.name: Ace of Pentacles
entries.body: A seed rests beside fresh farmland. The Ace of Pentacles offers a practical opening, with the tools and time needed to turn a possibility into something tangible.

entries.name: Two of Pentacles
entries.body: Two furnaces need tending as supplies change. The Two of Pentacles explores flexible balance, asking what rhythm helps your character manage competing needs.

entries.name: Three of Pentacles
entries.body: A mason, carpenter and planner share one workshop. The Three of Pentacles values learned skill, useful feedback and respect between different kinds of expertise.

entries.name: Four of Pentacles
entries.body: A storeroom stays locked when neighbors need supplies. The Four of Pentacles asks when careful keeping becomes a grip too tight to let resources serve their purpose.

entries.name: Five of Pentacles
entries.body: Two travelers pass a lit doorway in the snow. The Five of Pentacles gives hardship and exclusion room in the story, asking where welcome or practical help might be found.

entries.name: Six of Pentacles
entries.body: A supply chest opens for someone who needs a start. The Six of Pentacles considers giving and receiving, including who sets the terms and whether help preserves dignity.

entries.name: Seven of Pentacles
entries.body: An orchard grows slowly despite all the work already spent. The Seven of Pentacles pauses to assess progress: what needs more time, and what needs a different approach?

entries.name: Eight of Pentacles
entries.body: A craftsperson lines up a row of well-made tools. The Eight of Pentacles finds meaning in practice, patient attention and the small corrections that deepen a skill.

entries.name: Nine of Pentacles
entries.body: A well-kept garden offers shade earned through steady care. The Nine of Pentacles enjoys independence and cultivated comfort, with time to appreciate what has taken root.

entries.name: Ten of Pentacles
entries.body: A family base holds old maps, tools and rooms for newcomers. The Ten of Pentacles considers shared inheritance: what can this community leave useful to those who follow?

entries.name: Page of Pentacles
entries.body: A learner studies the soil before planting a sapling. The Page of Pentacles takes a practical interest seriously, turning curiosity into a small, attentive experiment.

entries.name: Knight of Pentacles
entries.body: Each morning, a farmer checks every field and closes every gate. The Knight of Pentacles honors reliability, while asking when a good routine needs an adjustment.

entries.name: Queen of Pentacles
entries.body: A kitchen holds bread, boots and room by the stove. The Queen of Pentacles makes care tangible, tending everyday needs without forgetting the person doing the tending.

entries.name: King of Pentacles
entries.body: A well-run granary supplies the village all winter. The King of Pentacles considers responsible stewardship, where lasting security matters more than displaying wealth.

sections.title: The Digits
sections.intro: Nine number characters to borrow for a scene, a question or a role.

entries.name: One
entries.body: One block marks a place where nothing stood before. One explores initiative and a distinct voice: what could your character begin without waiting for a leader?

entries.name: Two
entries.body: Two beds share a shelter, with room left between them. Two explores partnership and tact, asking how your character can hear a second voice without losing their own.

entries.name: Three
entries.body: Three colors become a banner worth showing a friend. Three explores expression and sociability: what takes shape when your character shares an idea beyond their thoughts?

entries.name: Four
entries.body: Four corner posts mark a shelter that can bear a roof. Four explores structure and dependable habits, asking what foundation helps ordinary days hold together.

entries.name: Five
entries.body: A trail branches into new country off the usual route. Five explores variety and change, including the freedom of experimenting and the difficulty of staying anywhere.

entries.name: Six
entries.body: A supper table needs food, chairs and someone noticing a gap. Six explores responsibility and care, asking how a household can include the needs of its caretaker.

entries.name: Seven
entries.body: A lone explorer records patterns in a cave notebook. Seven explores study and inward searching, asking what your character learns after staying with a question.

entries.name: Eight
entries.body: A busy trading hall turns decisions into consequences. Eight explores organization and power, asking how your character handles resources when others depend on them.

entries.name: Nine
entries.body: A departing builder leaves supplies in an open chest. Nine explores completion and generosity, asking what your character can release for a wider circle to inherit.

sections.title: Master Numbers
sections.intro: Three modern numerology motifs, widening partnership, structure and care.

entries.name: Eleven
entries.body: Two listeners compare faint sounds from a tunnel. Eleven heightens Two's sensitivity: let a subtle impression inspire a question, then leave room to check what was heard.

entries.name: Twenty-Two
entries.body: A long bridge needs a bold plan and firm supports. Twenty-Two widens Four's practical structure into work that serves many people and may outlast its first builders.

entries.name: Thirty-Three
entries.body: A builder opens a workshop for patient lessons. Thirty-Three widens Six's care through teaching, sharing a skill while keeping room for a life beyond helping.

closer.title: Leave a Light On
closer.body: Put the kettle by the furnace, leave a chair for a friend, and tuck the cards away when the story feels done. May your next little table have a good view and a cat underneath.
